brief: There is no agent-to-agent code anywhere in the source — no proximity test, no pairing, nothing. Every walker, gardener, café sitter and browser moves as though alone in the town, which is why the wide shot reads as traffic rather than as neighbours. Give agents the barest social awareness: when two of them pass close on the lane or on the courtyard ring, they should occasionally acknowledge each other — a pause, a turn of the head, a short stop to talk. Rare and brief is right; a town where everybody stops to chat is as wrong as one where nobody does.
successLooksLike: Watching the lane for a minute you see two people stop, face each other for a few seconds and move on, while the rest walk past each other as before. Census `people` is unchanged.
avoid: Do not run an O(n²) scan over a growing list every frame without a cheap distance reject first. Do not let a conversation deadlock a pair — `done` must stay reachable, because a stuck agent holds its café table via `tableRef` forever. Do not add a census field for this.
